verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever for about seven days with feeling hot, sweaty, and generally unwell: "I've been struggling with fever for the past week... really hot and sweaty all the time and just generally not feeling good."

Patient describes intermittent hot and cold spells and night sweats: "I'm sweating during the night. I'm quite cold" and "you're having periods of when you're feeling hot and also periods when you're feeling cold as well?" / "Yes... it's quite interchangeable."

Doctor asks about cough/cold/sore throat and ear pain and patient denies: "Have you got any cough or cold or sore throat, anything like that?" / Patient: "Not those sort of symptoms really" and later "Have you had an ear pain at all?" / Patient: "No, my ears are fine actually."
Patient reports generalized muscle aches: "I'd say that I'm aching all over, really. My muscles are really aching."
Patient reports nausea with poor intake: "I'm feeling quite nauseous, so I've not been able to eat very much and I have been drinking, but it's been quite a small amount."
Patient mentions fatigue: "Just generally quite tired and unwell."
Doctor: "Have you had any diarrhea?" Patient: "Not. Not really, no. I'm fine."
Doctor: "Have you got any neck stiffness at all?" Patient: "No."

Patient denies new/worse headache and describes baseline central headaches related to other triggers: "Do you have any headache?" / Patient: "Not more than usual, no... just like the general headaches... No migraines or anything." and "It's quite centralized over the head" and "It's something that I've struggled with for years."
Doctor: "have you got any rash in your body anywhere at all?" Patient: "I haven't noticed any rashes, no."

Doctor asks: "Any joints swollen or tender or sore?" Patient: "Not really. I mean, I often have problems with back pain, but not really any other joints?"—supports denial of joint swelling aside from chronic back pain.

Doctor asks about urinary symptoms including pain and frequency; patient denies: "have you got any kind of symptoms down below when you're passing urine?" / Patient: "No, there's been no problems there." and "Any painful urination at all?" / "Not at all, no." and "Are you passing urine more often than normal?" / "I don't think so, no."

Patient states return from Vietnam 4 weeks ago with mixed city and countryside, trekking/cycling through farmland: "I went to Vietnam. I came back four weeks ago now" and "we toured to several different parts of the country in the countryside and some cities as well" and "We were sort of trekking and cycling through farmland."

Patient took malaria prophylaxis, likely daily, but cannot recall name: "did you take malaria preventative medication" / "I did, yes"; "Was it a weekly tablet or a daily tablet?" / "I think it was daily"; "Which one do you take?" / "Oh, I can't remember now off the top of my head."

Patient reports an additional prophylaxis tablet: "was it one tablet or was there another one that you would take on top of the first one?" / Patient: "I think it was another one that I took on top of the first one."
Patient has chronic back pain managed by physiotherapy: "I often have problems with back pain" and later "Yes. Yeah. I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that."
Doctor: "Are you on any medication at all?" Patient: "Just ceraset."
Patient: "I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol just from over the counter... Just been taking the recommended dose every day of those."
Same quote supports ibuprofen use at recommended dose: "ibuprofen and paracetamol... Just been taking the recommended dose every day of those."

Patient allergic to pollen causing hay fever: "Do you have any allergies at all..." / Patient: "No, I'm just really. Pollen allergy, that's all I have." Doctor clarifies: "Okay, so hay fever?" / Patient: "Yes. Yeah, just hay fever."
Family history: "The main one would be heart attack. My. My father passed away of that." and "How old is he when that happens?" / "68, I think." Myocardial infarction = heart attack.
Occupation: "What do you work as?" / Patient: "I work as a nurse."
Smoking status: "are you a smoker at all?" / Patient: "No, I'm not."
Alcohol use: "And do you drink much alcohol?" / Patient: "Moderate alcohol intake? Drink too much."—supports moderate use with concern about amount.
Exercise: "And how much kind of physical exercise do you do normally?" / Patient: "I try and do some moderate physical exercise a few times a week."
Vaccinations: "you're up to date with all the vaccinations, Hepatitis B, that kind of thing?" / Patient: "Yes, indeed. Yeah."

Synthesis of history: 7 days of fever with night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and no clear source. Fever duration: "past week"; night sweats and chills: "I'm sweating during the night. I'm quite cold" with alternating hot/cold; myalgias: "aching all over... muscles are really aching"; nausea and low intake: "feeling quite nauseous"; no focal infection identified as per doctor's summary: "there's no apparent reason from what you've told me... we can't find a focus of infection."

Doctor explicitly links rural Vietnam travel with concern for malaria and exotic infections despite prophylaxis: "you've recently come from Vietnam and you've had exposure to rural areas, and we need to think about things like malaria or other exotic infections as well." Patient already stated taking prophylaxis.

Risk of dehydration is a direct inference from reduced intake: "I've not been able to eat very much and I have been drinking, but it's been quite a small amount." This reasonably supports concern for dehydration and impaired recovery.

Chronic low back pain is described and under physio; no mention of acute change: "I often have problems with back pain" and "I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that" with no report of worsening, supporting stable chronic condition.

Doctor proposes urgent in-person exam in central London today: "we're going to need to bring you into one of our clinics exam" and "You can come into one of our clinics in central London. That's one option" and patient agrees to come straight in today: "I can come straight into central London today to get that sorted."

Doctor plans blood tests after exam including malaria films and inflammatory markers: "we're going to need to arrange some blood tests as well" and "I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films to check for malaria and inflammatory markers and things like that." He notes tests depend on exam: "after you've been seen by somebody... which is why we're going to go for the examination first."
Work advice: "But I don't think you can go into work until we've sorted this out, and we need to sort this out sooner rather than later."

Alternative A&E plan: "if it's inconvenient for you to come into central London... you could actually just attend a local ae... I'm going to type up... what kind of tests I think you need... you could show that to them at reception. I'll be asking for... thick and thin blood films... and inflammatory markers."

Admin booking process and patient call-back are described: "I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in, and if you can, ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes after a few minutes and then they'll slot you in."
